issue.title: Glossary reference-task, reference-note, and area-note still describe in-note ^ref trackers

task_type_fields.proposed_change:
Update three glossary strands for the parent-residence reference model that epic bob-cli-5y shipped (plan:202610/ref_tasks_live_with_parent.md, research:202610/ref_tasks_move_into_parent_notes/ref_tasks_move_into_parent_notes.md; live migration commit 9253886 in the vault). The epic's auto decision memory_glossary_ref_terms = no forbade editing them during the epic; every phase (bob-cli-5y.1 through 5y.14) proposed this follow-up.

- `glossary/reference-task.md`: today it says the reference task is the single `#task` in the reference note identified by the exact trailing block ID `^ref`, linking to the PDF. Now: the single `#task #ref` reading task for a reference note, living in an area/project/inbox note's `## Tasks` (archived normally into `done/`), with a `^ref-<slug>` block ID that is only an address; identity is the `#ref` tag plus the path-qualified first link to the ref note; same mark mapping ([ ] ready, [*] next, [/] wip, [x] read, [-] abandoned, [?] blocked overlay). Keep the frozen in-note `^ref` form as the legacy/closed v1 shape.
- `glossary/reference-note.md`: holds no open tasks; shows its reading task through the managed embed `![[<residence>#^<id>]]` below the H1; frontmatter `parent` is projected from where that task lives (a done/ archive maps to that file's `parent:`). Annotation follow-ups default to the parent note.
- `glossary/area-note.md`: drop "a reference note's own [[reference-task]]" from the residence exceptions.

Coordinate with bob-cli-4n (reference-note follow-up-work phrase) and bob-cli-4t (area-note inbox routing wording): same files. Closing requires Bryan's permission plus `sase memory init` per the memory-write policy.

issue.creation_reason: Epic bob-cli-5y moved every open ref task into its parent note, but its auto decision memory_glossary_ref_terms=no left the glossary describing the retired in-note ^ref tracker; every phase proposed this follow-up.
